title: Research Trends in Machine Learning for Arabic Language Studies: A Bibliometric Analysis
abstract: This study aims to map the development of publications on the application of Machine Learning in Arabic language studies through bibliometric analysis. Research data was obtained from the Lens.org database and analyzed using VOSviewer software to identify publication trends, keyword networks, and research opportunities. The results show that the number of publications has increased significantly since 2015 and peaked in the 2020–2025 period. Keyword co-occurrence analysis shows that Machine Learning is a central theme closely related to deep learning, Arabic Natural Language Processing, classification, and Arabic Sentiment Analysis. Overlay visualizations show a shift in research focus from basic topics, such as translation, tagging, and text mining, to more sophisticated themes, such as Arabic hate speech, clustering, and ensemble learning. Meanwhile, density analysis indicates that Arabic Sign Language, FastText, Ensemble Learning, and Arabic Hate Speech still have a low publication density, thus potentially becoming future research directions. The findings of this study provide a comprehensive overview of the trends and developments in Machine Learning research in Arabic language studies and can serve as a reference for researchers in determining research themes and developing artificial intelligence-based innovations in Arabic language learning and processing.

title: Research on Novel Neural Networks: Semantic Energy Conservation Network (SEC-Net)
abstract: Modern deep neural networks often suffer from lack of interpretability, vanishing or exploding gradients, and representation collapse due to the absence of explicit physical or information-theoretic constraints during layer-wise feature transformations. To address these fundamental challenges, this paper proposes a novel architectural framework named the Semantic Energy Conservation Network (SEC-Net). The core philosophy of SEC-Net is inspired by the law of energy conservation in physics and rate-distortion theory in information theory. We define the total variance and representation capacity of the feature space at each layer as its "semantic energy." Unlike conventional networks where information undergoes uncontrolled entropy increase or degenerate entropy decrease, SEC-Net enforces an explicit layer-wise constraint to ensure that the semantic energy remains invariant throughout the feedforward propagation (E(H^(l+1)) = E(H^l)). This equilibrium is mathematically maintained through a dynamic rescaling mechanism and parameterized via orthonormal transformations. To preserve this structural integrity during optimization, we employ Riemannian Gradient Descent (RGD) on the Stiefel manifold coupled with a dynamic energy regularization loss, rather than standard Euclidean stochastic gradient descent. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that SEC-Net inherently bounds the spectral radius of the Jacobian matrices near unity, thereby fundamentally eliminating the root causes of gradient instability and removing the reliance on external normalization techniques like Batch Normalization. Furthermore, from an information-theoretic perspective, the strict control over entropy flow prevents representation collapse and allows the trajectory of semantic abstractions to be precisely tracked and interpreted across layers. This work provides a rigorous mathematical and conceptual foundation for stable, robust, and explainable deep learning architectures.

title: State-Aware Runtime for Long-Horizon LLM Agents: A Conceptual Framework and Research Agenda
abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents are increasingly expected to operate across extended interactions, evolving tasks, tool calls, memory updates, and multi-step plans. However, many failures in such systems are not adequately explained by single-turn reasoning errors or insufficient model capability. Instead, they arise from unstable state maintenance, uncontrolled memory injection, protocol drift, tool-mediated side effects, and missing recovery mechanisms. This paper defines State-Aware Runtime as the transaction-governance layer that separates model generation from canonical state, memory operations, validation, commit/rollback, and audit traces during execution. Its lifecycle includes boot-time initialization, session resume, baseline recovery, bounded state-view construction, proposal validation, commit, rollback or compensation, and audit. Stronger models may reduce the frequency of invalid proposals, but they do not remove the need for durable state, audit trails, permission boundaries, and side-effect governance when agent actions persist beyond a single model context. We provide a structured conceptual review of work on agent memory, tool use, long-context modeling, self-reflection, generative agents, workflow orchestration, and monitoring, and reorganize these strands around the problem of long-horizon runtime reliability. The central claim is that future agent reliability will depend less on prompt accumulation and more on explicit runtime systems that manage what the model is allowed to know, change, commit, forget, and recover. We conclude with a taxonomy of long-horizon failures and a research agenda for auditable, recoverable, and state-aware agent infrastructure.

title: Interleaved POMDP Planning for Multi-Object Search in Unknown Multi-Room Household Environments
abstract: Multi-object search in unknown household environments requires planning under extensive uncertainty - from unknown object locations to cluttered spaces with unobserved obstacles. POMDPs offer a principled framework for such problems but remain intractable in large domains. We propose Inter-POMDP, a novel interleaved POMDP planning algorithm that decomposes this challenge into two interacting levels: a high-level POUCT planner reasons over object distributions using LLM-informed histogram beliefs, while a low-level motion planner models navigation uncertainty with obstacle-aware particle beliefs as domain knowledge to guide high-level POUCT. This interleaved design balances planning quality and efficiency despite the large search space across unknown multi-room environments. Both simulation and real-world experiments show that our Inter-POMDP algorithm reduces collision counts by up to 63%, navigation steps by up to 35%, and detection counts by up to 32% compared with baseline methods. Full videos are https://sites.google.com/view/inter-pomdp

title: The evolution of AI from image interpretation toward scientific inference in nanoparticle electron microscopy
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming electron microscopy by enabling quantitative analysis of increasingly large and complex datasets for nanoparticle characterization. Recent advances in machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) have expanded microscopy from a descriptive imaging technique into a data-driven platform for structural interpretation, dynamic analysis, and scientific inference. This review examines AI methodologies for nanoparticle electron microscopy, focusing on transmission electron microscopy (TEM), high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM), scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), and in situ TEM. The discussion is organized around the principal challenges in nanoparticle characterization, including particle detection, segmentation, morphology quantification, atomic-resolution restoration, defect identification, two-dimensional-to-three-dimensional structural inference, and analysis of dynamic processes in situ. We review computational approaches from conventional ML and convolutional neural networks to transformer architectures, self-supervised learning, foundation models, multimodal AI, and physics-informed learning. We further discuss integrating microscopy data with simulations, metadata, and autonomous experimentation to relate nanoparticle structure, dynamics, synthesis conditions, and functional properties. The advantages, limitations, benchmarking, and data requirements of current methodologies are critically assessed. Finally, emerging opportunities for foundation models, AI-guided microscopy, closed-loop experimentation, and autonomous materials discovery are discussed. By integrating advances across computer vision, materials informatics, and electron microscopy, this review highlights the role of AI in next-generation nanoparticle characterization and accelerated materials discovery.

title: Sentimen Analisis Komentar Netizen pada Media Sosial Instagram terkait Sound Horeg dengan Metode LSTM dan BERT
abstract: ABSTRACT Sound horeg is a popular cultural phenomenon among young people, characterized by the use of large-capacity audio equipment during convoys and public entertainment. Its growing presence on Instagram has triggered diverse reactions from netizens through the comment section, ranging from positive, neutral, to negative sentiments. This study aims to determine the sentiment distribution of netizen comments toward the sound horeg phenomenon and to compare the performance of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) in classifying sentiment into three classes: positive, negative, and neutral. Data were collected through Instagram comment crawling using Selenium and BeautifulSoup, followed by bot validation, labeling, data augmentation using Synonym Replacement, and text preprocessing (cleaning, case folding, normalization, stopword removal, lemmatization, and tokenization). The LSTM model was built using a Sequential architecture with Embedding, LSTM, and Dense layers, while the BERT model used a fine-tuned IndoBERT Base P2 for three-class classification. Of 18,222 comments that passed bot validation, sentiment distribution was dominated by the negative class (78.2%), followed by other (9.9%), positive (7.2%), and neutral (4.7%). Results show that BERT consistently outperformed LSTM, achieving the highest accuracy of 87% without augmentation, while BERT with data augmentation achieved the best macro average F1-score of 0.55. These findings indicate that combining IndoBERT with Synonym Replacement augmentation is the most optimal configuration for handling class imbalance and informal language variation in social media comments.

title: Bounded Gödelian Language Models: Proof-Carrying, Survival-Satisficing Evolutionary Self-Adaptation
abstract: This paper introduces a survival-satisficing Gödelian learning machine that evolves self-modifying language-model progeny by prioritizing long-term viability, bounded operational well-being, and catastrophic-risk control over unconstrained utility maximization. The framework combines proof-carrying invariants, Lean/SMT verification, robust and risk-sensitive learning, evolutionary bet-hedging, and anytime-valid statistical certification, while adapting persistent self-edit mechanisms from recent self-adapting language models. By formalizing what it means for an LLM to be Gödelian and providing a reproducible architecture, algorithms, guarantees, and implementation sketches, the work offers a rigorous foundation for safer recursive self-improvement under uncertainty.

title: Research on Early Stopping during Inference: Inference-Time Computing Flow Optimization via Reasoning Redundancy Elimination (RRE)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting techniques, the accuracy of models in handling complex logical reasoning, mathematical theorems, and code generation has been significantly improved. However, this "thinking" mechanism, which trades longer reasoning steps for higher performance, inevitably introduces immense computational resource consumption during autoregressive decoding. In practical scenarios, models frequently suffer from the "reasoning redundancy" phenomenon, falling into repetitive logical loops, divergent invalid arguments, or generating a plethora of superfluous tokens irrelevant to the final answer. This drastically inflates Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) and generation costs per token, thereby hindering the feasibility of real-world deployment. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a non-intrusive early stopping framework named Reasoning Redundancy Elimination (RRE) for the inference phase. Without modifying the original parameters of the model, RRE introduces a lightweight dual-detection architecture during the decoding stage: the Semantic State Repetition Detector (SSRD) and the Dynamic Information Gain Evaluator (DIGE), which dynamically monitor the semantic trajectory and latent computational value of the generated reasoning steps. Once a reasoning segment is classified as low-value repetition, an invalid dead-end loop, or has reached a state of information convergence, RRE immediately sends an early stopping signal to the decoder, trims the redundant KV cache, and forces the model to jump directly to the final answer generation. Theoretical derivations and computational boundary analyses demonstrate that RRE substantially curtails invalid reasoning lengths and cuts down computational FLOPs exponentially while maintaining, or even improving, the final reasoning accuracy by eliminating error cascades in long-context generation. This framework offers a novel and promising paradigm for the highly efficient deployment of large language models.

title: From Commutants to Logical Control: Pre-Registered Verification of a Decoherence-Free Subspace on IBM Heron Processors
abstract: Protected Quantum Information on IBM Heron Processors: A Four-Experiment Pre-Registered Arc — Commutant Verification, Noise-Axis Characterization, Subspace Certification, and Logical Operation Under Interleaved Collective Rotations Date: July 10, 2026 Version: 2.1 (incorporates independent post-hoc review corrections; supersedes drafts 1.0/2.0) Related records: Phase 1 spatial Y⊗Z parity-consistency (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.18501679); correction record v1.3 (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20470129) Plain-language summary Quantum computers are extremely sensitive to noise — stray influences that corrupt the information they hold. But not all quantum information is equally fragile. If you store information in the right pattern across two qubits, certain kinds of disturbance pass through without changing it, the way a perfectly symmetric object looks unchanged in a mirror. Over four experiments on two IBM quantum processors (roughly two and a half minutes of total quantum computer time, as reported by our submission records), we asked four questions in order: Are the sign changes predicted by the protection math reproduced on real hardware? Yes. In all 42 individual circuit-level tests, deliberately applied disturbances flipped the stored signal exactly when the math said they would, and left its sign unchanged when the math said they should, with high measured contrast. Does the machine's own natural noise happen to be the kind this protection guards against? On the qubits we tested, no — and that is an important honest finding. The measured decay was consistent with energy leakage dominating over phase scrambling, so this particular protection does not help against the everyday noise we observed. We predicted the numbers in advance, and where our model was wrong, the record shows exactly what we corrected and when. Can a protected "safe pattern" be demonstrated directly? Yes. We prepared two states of similar complexity — one inside the protected pattern, one outside — and applied the same programmed disturbance to both. title: Hearing Like Humans? Sound Symbolism and Perceptual Alignment in Speech Language Models
abstract: Sound symbolism, the human tendency to map speech sounds to perceptual qualities such as roundness or sharpness, arises primarily from the acoustics of speech rather than spelling. Whether Speech Language Models (SLMs) share this tendency remains open, as prior evaluations rely on text or images rather than real speech. We study it using genuine human speech recordings, comparing model judgments against human data across the auditory, crossmodal, and visual components of the effect. We find that SLMs' auditory judgments align poorly with human perception and miss the acoustic cues, such as spectral tilt, that drive human intuitions, and open-weight models cannot reliably link a heard sound to its corresponding shape. With a visual-only control ruling out shape perception, the weakness localizes to how speech is represented, suggesting that perceptual alignment depends not on stronger vision but on speech representations that capture the cues humans hear.

title: Urgensi Pembaruan Regulasi Hak Cipta di Indonesia dalam Menjawab Hasil Karya Artificial Intelligence (AI)
abstract: This study aims to analyze the legal vacuum in copyright regulations regarding AI- generated works and examine the urgency of regulatory reform to address the challenges of this technological development. This study employs a prescriptive normative legal research method with a statutory approach and a conceptual approach. The legal materials used consist of primary and secondary legal materials collected through a literature review and analyzed using a qualitative descriptive method. The results of the study show that Law Number 28 of 2014 concerning Copyright is still oriented toward the concept of a human creator. As a result, works generated autonomously by AI do not meet the elements of creation required by law, thereby creating uncertainty regarding their ownership status and economic rights. Furthermore, the use of copyrighted works in the AI training process has the potential to cause copyright infringement. This study concludes that reforming copyright regulations is an urgent need through more adaptive regulations, including clarifying the liability of parties involved in AI development and usage, as well as regulating the equitable use of training data.

title: Analysis of the Knowledge Structure, Thematic Evolution, and Emerging and Future Research Directions in User Interface Design for Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) in Decision-Making Dashboards: A Scientometric Study
abstract: Purpose: The rapid diffusion of artificial intelligence (AI) in organizational decision environments has intensified concerns about transparency, interpretability, and user trust. As complex machine learning models increasingly support managerial and policy decisions, the need for Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) has become essential to ensure that decision makers understand and appropriately use algorithmic outputs. Decision dashboards have emerged as key interfaces through which AI driven insights are delivered to managers and analysts. Despite this growing importance, the intellectual structure and thematic evolution of XAI within decision dashboard design have not yet been systematically examined. The purpose of this study is therefore to analyze the knowledge structure, conceptual foundations, and thematic development of research on Explainable Artificial Intelligence in decision dashboards. Using scientometric techniques, the study identifies core research themes, emerging trends, and structural relationships shaping this rapidly developing field. It also highlights how technical developments in AI intersect with human centered design, decision support systems, and visualization approaches in explainable decision dashboards. Methodology: This study adopts a scientometric and bibliometric approach to map the intellectual landscape of XAI research in decision dashboards. Data were collected from the Scopus and Web of Science databases to ensure comprehensive coverage of peer reviewed literature. Following the PRISMA protocol for systematic screening and refinement, an initial dataset of 942 records was identified. After applying inclusion criteria and restricting the corpus to original research articles, 251 records from Scopus and 112 from Web of Science were retained. Duplicate and irrelevant records were removed, resulting in a final dataset of 269 articles. Data standardization and descriptive bibliometric analyses were conducted using the Bibliometrix package and the Biblioshiny interface. These tools enabled the examination of publication trends, leading journals, and author productivity patterns, including Bradford’s and Lotka’s laws. To explore the conceptual structure of the field, keyword co occurrence network analysis was performed using VOSviewer. Network, density, and overlay visualizations were generated to identify thematic clusters, intellectual linkages, and temporal changes in research topics. Additionally, thematic evolution mapping and logistic growth modeling were applied to examine the developmental trajectory of the field. Findings: The findings show that research on Explainable Artificial Intelligence in decision dashboards is evolving from a purely technical and algorithm centered domain toward a multidimensional and interdisciplinary knowledge structure. Co occurrence analysis reveals that the intellectual core of the field is organized around three central concepts: Explainable AI, decision making, and deep learning. These themes form the primary hub of the conceptual network, indicating that explainability is increasingly recognized as a fundamental component of intelligent decision support systems rather than a supplementary feature of machine learning models. The results also reveal several interconnected thematic clusters, including human ethical considerations, technical methodological development, applied operational contexts, cognitive autonomous systems, and emerging specialized topics. This structure reflects the convergence of two complementary research logics: algorithmic performance and engineering efficiency on the one hand, and human understanding, trust, and accountability on the other. Density visualization confirms that the highest concentration of research lies at the intersection of Explainable AI, decision making, and deep learning, highlighting the central role of deep learning technologies in the field. However, these technologies require integration with interpretability mechanisms and user interface design to be effective in decision dashboards. Overlay visualization further indicates a thematic transition over time. Earlier research focused on classical machine learning techniques such as neural networks and support vector machines, whereas recent studies increasingly emphasize visual deep learning, visualization techniques, trust, and intelligent decision support systems. Another key finding is that concepts such as trust and visualization have moved from peripheral topics to integral components of XAI systems, emphasizing the growing importance of user comprehension and interaction in AI supported decision processes. Logistic growth modeling also indicates that the field remains in a rapid expansion phase and has not yet reached scientific saturation. Conclusion: The results demonstrate that the research landscape of Explainable Artificial Intelligence in decision dashboards is shifting from a technology centered paradigm toward a human and decision centered paradigm. Explainability is increasingly understood not only as a technical capability that clarifies algorithmic outputs but also as a cognitive bridge between complex AI systems and human decision makers. The findings highlight that the effectiveness of AI enabled decision dashboards depends not only on predictive accuracy but also on the ability of systems to communicate reasoning processes in an interpretable and trustworthy manner. Consistent with previous studies, the practical value of explainable AI emerges when explanations enhance transparency, foster user trust, and support informed decision making in complex environments. By mapping the intellectual structure and thematic evolution of this interdisciplinary domain, the study provides insights into its conceptual foundations and future research directions. In particular, it emphasizes the importance of integrating deep learning technologies with explainability mechanisms, visualization techniques, and human centered interface design to develop effective decision dashboards.

title: A Reproducible Toolkit for GF(2^5) Encoding and Reed–Solomon Error Correction of Synthetic Biopolymer Data
abstract: This record contains an open, tested Python toolkit and accompanying preprint forencoding amino-acid sequences into the finite Galois field GF(2^5) = GF(32) andprotecting them with a working Reed–Solomon error-correcting codec. The toolkit provides: (i) a self-contained GF(2^k) arithmetic engine (GF(2), GF(4),GF(16), GF(32)) verified exhaustively against the field axioms; (ii) a completesystematic Reed–Solomon codec over GF(32), block length 31, with Berlekamp–Massey,Chien-search, and Forney decoding; and (iii) an end-to-end pipeline that encodes anamino-acid message, protects it, passes it through a symbol-substitution channel, andrecovers it. A demonstration recovers a 30-residue insulin B-chain peptide exactly atchannel error probabilities up to 0.10. Scope and honest framing: this is engineering infrastructure, not a new coding result.It does NOT claim that the biochemical organisation of the encoding improves errorcorrection — it does not, and the package includes the tests that establish this, becausestandard Reed–Solomon decoding depends only on the number of symbol errors, not theiridentity. The work builds on and cites prior finite-field coding of biological sequences(the Faria–Palazzo BCH line) and Reed–Solomon coding for molecular communication(Dissanayake et al., 2017). The contribution is a clean, verified, reusable openimplementation. evidence.title: A Reproducible Toolkit for GF(2^5) Encoding and Reed–Solomon Error Correction of Synthetic Biopolymer Data
evidence.abstract: This record contains an open, tested Python toolkit and accompanying preprint forencoding amino-acid sequences into the finite Galois field GF(2^5) = GF(32) andprotecting them with a working Reed–Solomon error-correcting codec. title: The Universal Syzygy Principle: A Hexad Summary A Speculative Design Proposal for Confidence-Gated Quantum Control, with an Analogical Borrowing from Relational Dynamics
abstract: This Hexad Summary outlines a proposed architecture connecting ideas from three separate areas: (i) an analogical borrowing of the coupling ratio ρ= Φ−1 ≈0.618 from Kain’s psychological/multi-agent relational dynamics model (Kain, 2026), where it appears strictly as a chosen, non-derived parameter; (ii) a proposed five-register compiler architecture (Spatial, Motion, Interaction, Confidence, Syzygy) for quantum control; and (iii) a proposed FPGA-based confidence-gated readout implementing erasure-preferential error management. No part of this architecture has been built, simulated, or empirically tested. The Universal Syzygy Principle – that coherence emerges from continuous relational balance rather than discrete threshold enforcement – is presented here as a design hypothesis for fault-tolerant quantum control, not as an established or validated result.

title: Context-Effect Study (2026-07)
abstract: This component holds the 2026-07 context-effect study: a preregistered within-item paired ablation testing whether prompt-level context (participant names, biographical background, and domain vocabulary) improves language-model ASR accuracy on digitized oral-history cassette audio. Archival interview audio from a deployed transcription tool is reprocessed through two large-language-model ASR systems (OpenAI gpt-4o-transcribe and Google gemini-2.5-flash) with the acoustic model held fixed, varying only the context prompt across three conditions (none, generic structure only, full context), and scored against human-produced verbatim references using word/character error rate and beyond-WER measures (named-entity fidelity and context-induced over-biasing). This component contains the preregistration, the hash-verified frozen analysis code, and the derived results; personal data (audio, participant names, transcripts) is held out of the public record. The confirmatory analysis covers 19 interview sides across the two models.

title: Analisis Explainability Pada Klasifikasi Citra Wayang Kulit Pandawa dan Punakawan Menggunakan MobileNetV3-Small dan EfficientNet-B0
abstract: Deep learning models such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) achieve high predictive performance, but their black-box nature makes their decision-making processes difficult to interpret. This study aims to compare the performance of MobileNetV3-Small and EfficientNet-B0 architectures in classifying images of Pandawa and Punakawan wayang kulit (shadow puppet) characters, and to analyze the visual features underlying each model's decisions through an eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) approach. The dataset consisted of 966 wayang images across eight character classes, obtained through data scraping. Both models were trained using transfer learning and fine-tuning, and evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score metrics. Explainability analysis was conducted using feature ablation and Grad-CAM to identify the contribution of color, texture, and shape features, as well as the image regions that most influenced each model's predictions. The results show that EfficientNet-B0 achieved an accuracy of 87%, outperforming MobileNetV3-Small, which achieved 82%, while also demonstrating better generalization ability. The feature ablation results indicate that shape features contributed the most to classification decisions in both models, while Grad-CAM visualizations revealed that the models relied on distinctive visual attributes such as crowns, faces, and clothing of the wayang characters. Both models were able to distinguish the Pandawa and Punakawan groups effectively, but still faced difficulties with visually similar characters such as Arjuna, Yudhistira, and NakulaSadewa. Overall, EfficientNet-B0 proved superior to MobileNetV3-Small in both accuracy and interpretability for wayang image classification.

title: Research on Random Forest Variant: Graph Reconstruction Forest (GRF) — Theory and Applications
abstract: Ensemble learning, as a core domain of machine learning, constructs strong learners by combining multiple weak learners and has demonstrated exceptional robustness and generalization capabilities in classification, regression, and feature selection tasks. Random Forest (RF) stands out as a classic representative of ensemble learning. Its essence lies in executing dual random sampling across both sample and feature spaces to build a highly diverse ensemble of decision trees. However, traditional Random Forests encounter fundamental bottlenecks when processing structured data, topological relationships, and graph data in non-Euclidean spaces, as they struggle with node representation, lose graph topological information, and lack the capacity for dynamic network reconstruction. To address these critical limitations, the Graph Reconstruction Forest (GRF) has emerged as a novel paradigm. As a topological ensemble learning method designed specifically for graph learning and network topology inference, the core philosophy of GRF is to transform the traditional scalar feature-splitting mechanism of Random Forests into high-dimensional topological feature reconstruction and graph structure regeneration. Within the GRF framework, nodes in the base decision trees no longer represent simple scalar thresholds of features; instead, they represent the projection and partitioning of graph structures within multi-scale feature subspaces. Concurrently, the leaf nodes generate localized structural features with high similarity through a specialized aggregation mechanism. Ultimately, GRF performs a non-linear ensemble averaging over the outputs of all decision trees in the forest, thereby achieving accurate learning of latent node embeddings and high-dimensional topological reconstruction of unknown graph structures. This paper provides a systematic and in-depth theoretical study and architectural derivation of the Graph Reconstruction Forest. First, we outline the evolutionary logic from traditional Random Forest to GRF, revealing its unique advantages in the realm of graph learning. Second, we systematically derive the mathematical mechanisms of GRF, including its node topological representation, splitting criteria based on graph reconstruction error, the structural aggregation mechanism of leaf nodes, and the overarching algorithmic framework. Third, we conduct comprehensive theoretical analysis across four dimensions: computational complexity, topological fidelity, algorithmic convergence, and robustness against noise and missing edges. Finally, we explore the extensive application scenarios of GRF in biological network inference, hidden link prediction in social networks, and geometric graph reconstruction in 3D point clouds. This research establishes a solid theoretical foundation and methodological guidance for applying ensemble learning to topological inference on non-Euclidean data.

title: The Actualizer Engine & Fractal Deduction Search Algorithm (FDSA): A Unified Top-Down Pre-Inference Steering Framework for Factual Grounding in Parallel Attention Transformers
abstract: Executive Summary: What is New in V3 (v3 / V3_U1 Update) The V3 / V3_U1 update unifies the standalone core engines (FDSA, QCA, and Actualizer) into a production-grade orchestrator pipeline (ActualizerFDSAQCAPipeline), establishes mathematical proofs for canonical stage execution, introduces dual-mode steering, and expands the benchmark suite. 1. Unified Pipeline Architecture (ActualizerFDSAQCAPipeline) Single Unified Orchestrator: Replaces disconnected script calls with a single pipeline class (ActualizerFDSAQCAPipeline) and factory functions (create_sequential_pipeline, create_parallel_pipeline). Canonical 3-Stage Pipeline: Stage 1 (FDSA Pruning): Domain isomorphic anchoring & grammar masking. Stage 2 (QCA Parallel Partitioning): RGG quench-clustering (TqRGGTqRGG) partitioning active nodes into KK parallel clusters. Stage 3 (Actualizer Final Snap): Banach contractive steering & causal snap gating (Tr(Dμν)≤τbifurcationTr(Dμν)≤τbifurcation). 2. Theoretical Advancement: Theorem 2.1 (Ordinal Canonicality) Theorem 2.1 (Proof of Stage Ordering): Mathematically proves and empirically verifies that pre-inference logit pruning (FDSA) MUST strictly precede Banach steering (Actualizer): FDSA⟶QCA⟶Actualizer, FDSA⟶QCA⟶Actualizer Arithmetic Savings: Executing Actualizer before FDSA forces contractive loops over the full unpruned vocabulary V, wasting ~99.85% of arithmetic operations on unviable tokens. Pre-pruning eliminates dead tokens before the contraction loop begins. 3. Latency Optimizations & Multi-Backend Parallelism Dual-Mode Cluster Steering: "fast" mode (default): 3-step drift-aware Banach iteration computing future drift Dfuture(v)=∣ln⁡U(v)+1.0∣Dfuture(v)=∣lnU(v)+1.0∣ and Vacuum Brake decay (∼0.5ms/cluster∼0.5ms/cluster). "full" mode: Complete Banach contraction loop until L2 convergence δ≤Qcδ≤Qc (∼5ms/node∼5ms/node). Persistent ThreadPool Backend: Replaces process-spawn IPC overhead on Windows with persistent multi-threading, delivering up to 60× speedup over process spawn (25ms total Stage 2 latency at N=240N=240). Multi-Backend Support: Dynamic fallback across threads (ThreadPool), jax (SIMD/GPU), and processes (multiprocessing). title: Sentiment Analysis for Patient Satisfaction Assessment in Bilingual E-Pharmacy Platforms
abstract: Patient-generated content has grown significantly as e-pharmacy continues to grow quickly, especially in China, which has one of the biggest and most vibrant online pharmacy ecosystems. Product reviews are one of the most important categories of user-generated data since they offer authentic, experience-based insights straight from patient. These reviews have an impact on business-level planning, product development strategies, and general market trends in addition to individual purchasing decisions. Despite their significance, product reviews are difficult to analyze because of their unstructured nature and the linguistic diversity of customers around the world. Every day, millions of reviews are posted on Chinese e-commerce sites like Taobao, JD.com, Tmall, and Pinduoduo. Cross-lingual sentiment analysis is challenging for researchers from around the world because many of these reviews are written in Chinese. In order to get around this obstacle, the current study uses well-known Natural Language Processing (NLP) tools and machine learning techniques to conduct a comparative and standardized analysis of Chinese product reviews that have been translated into English. People still talk about how the BERT-based classifier really stood out among all the models. The results make it clear that BERT hits an impressive 98.10 percent accuracy and F1 score of 0.972. This NLP model outperforms the traditional models.

title: Effectiveness of Intermediate-Task Training for Zero-Shot Code Generation Transfer
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. title: Self-Explaining Weight Generator Network: A Novel Paradigm for Intrinsic Interpretability via Dynamic Weight Generation
abstract: Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) have achieved remarkable success across various domains, yet their inherently opaque "black-box" nature remains a major obstacle for deployment in safety-critical applications. Traditional post-hoc explanation methods only provide approximations of a trained model and fail to reflect the true internal decision-making mechanism. To bridge the gap between model performance and interpretability, this paper proposes a novel architectural paradigm named the Self-Explaining Weight Generator Network (SEW-Net). Unlike conventional networks that directly learn and fix static weight tensors, SEW-Net introduces an independent Explanation Generator Network (EGN) alongside a Main Task Network (MTN). For any given input sample x, the EGN dynamically generates the specific weight matrices W_x for the MTN based on underlying human-understandable concepts, rather than relying on fixed connections. By structuring the generation process as a combination of globally shared basis tensors modulated by localized concept activations c(x), the runtime weights themselves serve as the most faithful, first-order local explanations. Furthermore, we introduce three core optimization constraints—local smoothness, concept sparsity, and basis orthogonality—to prevent the network from degenerating into an uninterpretable hypernetwork. We present the comprehensive mathematical formulation of SEW-Net, derive its forward and backward propagation workflows using multi-variable chain rules, and analytically evaluate its theoretical merits. Our analysis demonstrates that SEW-Net not only achieves 100% faithful, multi-layered intrinsic explanations without sacrificing non-linear expressiveness, but also offers enhanced theoretical robustness against adversarial perturbations and superior compositional generalization in low-data regimes.

title: Research on Contrastive Random Forest (CRF) Based on Maximizing Path Discrepancy
abstract: Random Forest (RF), as one of the most representative ensemble learning algorithms in the field of machine learning, has been widely utilized in classification, regression, and feature selection tasks due to its outstanding anti-overfitting capability, high-dimensional data handling capacity, and excellent generalization performance. However, traditional random forests rely heavily on localized splitting criteria based on purity metrics such as Gini impurity or information gain during decision tree construction. While this strategy effectively extracts the common features within a single class, it often struggles to fully uncover the deep structural differences and latent adversarial features between samples when dealing with high-level noise, blurred class boundaries, or complex non-linear manifolds. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel random forest variant termed Contrastive Random Forest (CRF). Distinct from existing methods that decouple contrastive learning as a data augmentation or pre-text feature extraction mechanism, CRF deeply integrates the contrastive mechanism directly into the parallel growth and splitting process of decision trees. During the construction of a single forest, CRF simultaneously tracks and learns the routing trajectories of positive samples (positive path flows) and negative samples (negative path flows) within the decision tree network. By designing a dedicated path discrepancy metric, the algorithm explicitly maximizes the global topological discrepancy between positive and negative paths during node splitting. This paper systematically elucidates the core concepts of CRF, details the mathematical formulation of the splitting criterion based on path discrepancy maximization, and establishes a complete framework for decision tree splitting and forest ensemble. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that CRF effectively expands the separation distance between different classes in the underlying manifold space, significantly enhancing the model's discriminative power against complex decision boundaries. This study provides a fresh paradigm for the profound integration of ensemble learning and contrastive representation.

title: From Interaction Topology to Realized Context: Diagnosing Exposure in LLM-Agent Social Simulation
abstract: Social simulation provides a controlled framework for studying opinion evolution and collective behavior. Recent LLM-agent simulators extend this paradigm through natural-language interactions. However, real individuals do not process all socially available information. Limited attention and bounded context mean that only part of the available evidence becomes behaviorally effective. Existing simulators face the same challenge: interaction graphs specify who can potentially communicate, but agent updates depend on which information is ultimately exposed to the LLM. We formalize this distinction as the interaction-exposure gap, and model graph-coupled simulation as an exposure-conditioned state-transition process. Interaction topology constrains available social evidence, while an exposure operator determines which evidence enters the agent-visible context. This view treats exposure as an explicit interface connecting network structure to LLM-driven behavior and enables controlled exposure interventions under otherwise matched simulation settings. Across controlled probes and two representative simulation workloads, exposure choices consistently affect individual updates, collective dynamics, and trajectory alignment. Recipient-conditioned exposure substantially changes trajectory alignment, reducing opinion-trajectory MAE from 0.402 to 0.115. These results suggest that social outcomes in LLM-agent simulation depend not only on who can interact, but also on which available information is actually presented to agents.

title: CAFE: A Compound-AI Factorial Evaluation Framework
abstract: We introduce CAFE (Compound-AI Factorial Evaluation), an open-source platform that brings design of experiments to the evaluation of compound AI systems (CAIS). Such systems expose many interchangeable choices - e.g. which retriever, model, or prompt - and practitioners rarely know which of them most affects answer quality. With CAFE, a practitioner registers each swappable component of a pipeline as a factor to build a factorial design over the chosen factors, run the resulting configurations, and score the answers on a shared rubric using a configurable LLM judge together with human raters. From these ratings it attributes answer-quality variance to the components and their interactions with mixed-effects models and reports effect sizes, significance, the best configuration, cost and latency trade-offs, and judge-human reliability. Whereas existing tools mostly either search for a good configuration or score outputs in isolation, CAFE also explains which component drives quality and whether an observed difference is significant. We validate CAFE on a retrieval-augmented question-answering (QA) pipeline over the HotpotQA benchmark dataset, where it recovers planted factor effects and stays calibrated under a permutation null. CAFE is released as a Python package and as a Web application.

title: Beyond Static Semantic Representation: A Conceptual Perspective on Structured Semantic Organization
abstract: Modern language models are commonly described in terms of static representations together with discrete computational operations. This perspective has proven highly successful for many applications, yet it may not fully capture every observable aspect of semantic computation. This paper proposes a conceptual perspective in which semantic organization is treated as a source of structured computational behavior that cannot always be adequately characterized by static representation alone. Rather than introducing a specific implementation, mathematical formulation, computational architecture, or operational procedure, the present work focuses exclusively on the conceptual proposition, its observable consequences, and its empirical falsifiability. Preliminary internal investigations motivated this perspective by revealing reproducible distinctions between semantically organized conditions and appropriately constructed control conditions under repeated evaluation. The reported observations suggest that semantic organization may contribute to computational phenomena that remain systematically distinguishable beyond what would be expected from arbitrary numerical organization alone. The present article intentionally does not disclose the realization responsible for these observations. The contribution of this work is therefore conceptual rather than technical. It establishes a falsifiable research direction, defines observable predictions suitable for independent examination, and documents the existence of an implemented but undisclosed research program supporting the conceptual proposal. Technical realization, mathematical formulation, implementation details, evaluation procedures, and engineering artifacts are intentionally reserved for future publications.

title: DICOM Converted and Original MRXS Whole Slide Images of Paired Hematoxylin-Eosin +/- Saffron Canine Breast Cancer Specimens
abstract: Overview. This dataset contains DICOM converted and original MRXS Whole Slide Images of canine breast cancer specimens with paired Hematoxylin-Eosin with and without Saffron staining, described in the scientific paper [1]. The source dataset comprises seven canine breast cancer specimens prepared as HE slides then additionally stained with Saffron. Both versions of the slides were scanned at 20x (approx. 0.0005mm per pixel) with a 3DHistech Panoramic Scan II, as described in the original paper [1]. The source images were shared in the proprietary MRXS form, and then converted to DICOM using the 3DHISTECH SlideMaster [2] software (v3.1.0.254167) with a temporary license provided by the vendor. The conversion tool properties were configured to write TILED_FULL DICOM images with Extended Offset Tables. Additional metadata was then added describing the subject (patient) and specimen preparation using the open source com.pixelmed.apps.SetCharacteristicsFromSummary tool [3] with the information derived from the original paper and the source file name, using the Bourne shell script in this collection. Specimens and slides and scans were acquired at Veterinärmedizinische Universität Wien, and are publicly shared (CC-BY-4.0) with the permission of Tribun Health, who sponsored the original study [1]. Notes. Though mathematically lossless conversion of proprietary WSI format to DICOM is often possible by using the original compressed tiles [4], the MRXS files contain overlapping tiles, so the conversion to the conventional non-overlapped DICOM TILED_FULL representation is inherently lossy due to (a) the resolution of overlapping as well as (b) the decompression and recompression cycle required for re-rendering; both of these factors are affected by the specific converter code and settings used; see the discussion in [5]. The source MRXS files are provided in case the recipient wants to directly access the original tiles, or use alternative converters, such as wsidicomizer [6], which supports MRXS and rendering of overlapping tiles through the use of the OpenSlide reader [7]. The LABEL and THUMBNAIL images in the vendor-converted DICOM series appear to contain inconsistencies with respect to the size measurements as reported by dciodvfy [8], so caution should be taken interpreting these values. evidence.title: DICOM Converted and Original MRXS Whole Slide Images of Paired Hematoxylin-Eosin +/- Saffron Canine Breast Cancer Specimens
evidence.abstract: Overview. This dataset contains DICOM converted and original MRXS Whole Slide Images of canine breast cancer specimens with paired Hematoxylin-Eosin with and without Saffron staining, described in the scientific paper [1]. The source dataset comprises seven canine breast cancer specimens prepared as HE slides then additionally stained with Saffron. Both versions of the slides were scanned at 20x (approx. 0.0005mm per pixel) with a 3DHistech Panoramic Scan II, as described in the original paper [1]. The source images were shared in the proprietary MRXS form, and then converted to DICOM using the 3DHISTECH SlideMaster [2] software (v3.1.0.254167) with a temporary license provided by the vendor. The conversion tool properties were configured to write TILED_FULL DICOM images with Extended Offset Tables. Additional metadata was then added describing the subject (patient) and specimen preparation using the open source com.pixelmed.apps.SetCharacteristicsFromSummary tool [3] with the information derived from the original paper and the source file name, using the Bourne shell script in this collection. Specimens and slides and scans were acquired at Veterinärmedizinische Universität Wien, and are publicly shared (CC-BY-4.0) with the permission of Tribun Health, who sponsored the original study [1]. Notes. Though mathematically lossless conversion of proprietary WSI format to DICOM is often possible by using the original compressed tiles [4], the MRXS files contain overlapping tiles, so the conversion to the conventional non-overlapped DICOM TILED_FULL representation is inherently lossy due to (a) the resolution of overlapping as well as (b) the decompression and recompression cycle required for re-rendering; both of these factors are affected by the specific converter code and settings used; see the discussion in [5]. The source MRXS files are provided in case the recipient wants to directly access the original tiles, or use alternative converters, such as wsidicomizer [6], which supports MRXS and rendering of overlapping tiles through the use of the OpenSlide reader [7]. The LABEL and THUMBNAIL images in the vendor-converted DICOM series appear to contain inconsistencies with respect to the size measurements as reported by dciodvfy [8], so caution should be taken interpreting these values. title: Poisoning LLM Agent Memory via Web Content
abstract: LLM agents are becoming increasingly capable, with systems such as OpenClaw combining tool use, web retrieval, and persistent memory. This capability raises a new security concern: untrusted web content may induce the agent to write malicious information into MEMORY.md. We call this risk web-derived memory contamination. To study this problem, we build an OpenClaw simulator and evaluate eight backend LLMs under two web-retrieval scenarios and five prompt-injection strategies. Our results show that six models write attacker-influenced content into memory in at least one setting. Such contaminated memory may later be loaded during unrelated tasks and trigger unsafe agent behavior, indicating that memory writes should be treated as security-sensitive operations rather than ordinary model outputs.

title: Service robot led by Mr. John: the mere disclosure human leader effect
abstract: Purpose Although robots have become increasingly intelligent, they face difficulties in gaining competence recognition when entering the service industry. The purpose of this paper is to introduce and test a novel, simple and low-cost strategy for mitigating consumers’ competence bias towards service robots. Design/methodology/approach Based on social categorization theory, this paper investigates whether the mere disclosure of the human leader of service robots (DHL) helps improve consumers’ evaluation of the robots’ competence by changing their categorization of service robots relative to human employees, as well as its boundary condition and downstream consequence. Four experimental studies were conducted to test the conceptual model across multiple service scenarios and robot types. Findings Study 1 demonstrates that DHL can effectively enhance consumers’ perceived competence of service robots. Study 2 further reveals the underlying mechanism of in-group identification. Study 3 identifies consumers’ construal level as a theoretically derived moderator. Moreover, Study 4 reveals the positive downstream effect of DHL on consumers’ intention to use service robots, thus highlighting the practical value of the DHL strategy. Research limitations/implications This research advances existing literature on strategies to mitigate consumers’ competence bias towards service robots. Practical implications This research offers concrete and actionable practical implications: companies can simply disclose the human leader of service robots (i.e. the DHL strategy) to mitigate consumers’ competence bias, thereby encouraging consumers to accept and use service robots in scenarios such as retail, catering and customer service. Originality/value This research introduces a novel DHL strategy to mitigate consumers’ competence bias towards service robots and offers a new social categorization perspective for understanding algorithm aversion.

title: Identity-Consistent Expression Fields: A Disentangled Neural Radiance Field Framework for Few-Shot Facial Expression Synthesis
abstract: Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) have enabled photorealistic novel-view synthesis of 3D scenes and, in the facial domain, have been extended to reconstruct and animate 3D face models from a small number of images. However, existing few-shot dynamic NeRF methods for facial expression editing typically warp a single learned feature volume conditioned on target expression parameters, which can cause identity-specific appearance details (skin texture, fine geometric structure) to drift when the model is driven toward expressions far from those seen in the few-shot input set. We propose Identity-Consistent Expression Fields (ICEF), a framework that explicitly disentangles a static, identity-specific radiance component from a dynamic, expression-conditioned deformation component, and introduces an identity preservation regularizer that constrains the deformation network to modify only expression-relevant regions while leaving identity-specific canonical appearance untouched. ICEF further incorporates a confidence-weighted conditional feature warping step that down-weights unreliable warps for target expressions that are far, in parameter space, from the observed few-shot inputs, mitigating artifacts observed in prior few-shot dynamic NeRF methods when extrapolating to novel expressions. We relate ICEF to prior few-shot dynamic NeRF, static 3D-aware face generation, and disentangled face-editing radiance field methods, and describe an evaluation protocol measuring both novel-expression rendering quality and, specifically, identity-consistency metrics across a range of expression-parameter extrapolation distances.

title: Impact of Intermediate-Task Training Order on Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Performance in XTREME-R
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. title: The Coherence Engine: Exploring the Space of Coherent Structures
abstract: This work introduces the coherence engine, a computational framework for constructing and executing coherent structures in the untyped λ-calculus. Beginning from stochastic β-reduction under finite reduction budgets, the framework generates coherent chains that admit recursive collapse into compact computational representations. We show that independently generated chains compose through junctions satisfying a non-divergence property, giving rise to feed-forward and recurrent coherent structures with convergent execution. This work develops the computational theory of coherent structures and serves as a companion to The Universal Explainer, which investigates how such structures acquire physical meaning through representational theories.

title: Model-Guided Routing Optimization of Superconducting Quantum Chips Tailored for qLDPC Codes
abstract: bivariate bicycle (BB) codes can lower qubit overhead for fault-tolerant computation, but their nonlocal checks are hard to route on planar superconducting chips. We study bottom-level BB-code routing under occupancy, crossing, and edge availability constraints. Our framework compares greedy best-first and beam routing with a fully convolutional model trained from lookahead rewards. The model predicts directional probability maps for graph-search expansion, while explicit checks enforce feasibility and evaluate cost. Under the current cost model, model-guided routing reduces average total cost by 31.5%, 4.1%, 3.4%, and 2.4% over initial, greedy, beam, and random-prior baselines. The results show that learning-guided search improves routing quality while feasibility is still enforced by explicit constraint checks.

title: AdaKG-RAG: Adaptive KG-guided retrieval-augmented generation with hypothesis-and-verification retrieval for multi-hop question answering
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has improved the factual grounding of large language models, but multi-hop question answering remains challenging because a system may retrieve semantically relevant yet evidence-incomplete contexts. Existing KG-guided RAG methods improve evidence coverage through graph expansion, but they often operate in a single-pass manner and lack an explicit mechanism for judging whether the assembled evidence is sufficient for reliable reasoning. Therefore, we propose AdaKG-RAG, an evidence-sufficiency-driven KG-guided RAG framework for multi-hop question answering. The core of AdaKG-RAG is a Hypothesis-and-Verification Retrieval (HVR) loop, which first forms a tentative answer from the current evidence, verifies whether the evidence is sufficient, and triggers targeted retrieval refinement when bridge facts are missing. To support this loop, AdaKG-RAG uses semantic-aware KG expansion and path-aware evidence organization to recover and structure candidate bridge evidence, followed by answer-aware supporting-fact (SF) reranking for better answer–evidence alignment. Experiments on HotpotQA and MuSiQue, together with a long-context evaluation on TriviaQA, show that AdaKG-RAG improves both answer quality and evidence retrieval quality over representative RAG and KG-RAG baselines. Further analysis indicates that HVR contributes the largest performance gain, while graph-based modules provide complementary improvements in evidence coverage and organization.

title: Robotic Contextual Awareness for Human-Robot Collaboration and Environmental Understanding
abstract: The transition of autonomous mobile robots from controlled industrial settings to dynamic, human-centric environments, such as manufacturing, logistics, and healthcare, has made their safe and autonomous operation a critical area of research. These sophisticated machines must be capable of perceiving, understanding, and interacting with their surroundings to navigate freely and perform complex tasks. A significant obstacle to achieving this is the lack of comprehensive contextual awareness, which requires a robot to recognize its spatial environment and identify the objects and actors within it. Without this perceptual knowledge, robots struggle to plan adaptive behaviors or engage in meaningful interaction with humans. This thesis presents novel solutions to this challenge by exploring two distinct but complementary research directions. The first direction involves human re-identification and tracking to improve Human-Robot Collaboration. Our developed approach enables a mobile robot to recognize a specific person, facilitating targeted collaboration while ignoring other individuals. The second direction focuses on enhancing the robot's overall perceptual capabilities to understand its environment geometrically and semantically. Geometric information is vital for motion planning and collision avoidance, while semantic knowledge provides the robot with a richer understanding for more advanced interaction. Both solutions are driven by the improvement of the semantical understanding of robots that enhance their knowledge of their surroundings, allowing a smoother and more natural interaction between robots, humans, and the environment. The contributions of this work in human re-identification and environmental understanding represent a significant step toward a future where robots are more contextually aware, enabling safer coexistence and more effective collaboration.

title: Convergent Hallucination in Multi-LLM Consensus: A Two-Layer Guard with Empirical Evidence in UK/EU Regulated Domains
abstract: Multi-LLM consensus systems are increasingly deployed in regulated professional services (immigration advisory, financial compliance, medical, legal), where practitioners hope that agreement among independent models will reduce hallucination risk. We document the opposite failure: when sub-models share overlapping training corpora with stale snapshots of a regulated domain, they converge on the same fabrication, and semantic-agreement scoring correctly reports high confidence in the wrong answer. On 2026-06-28, six sub-models produced 5-out-of-5 fabricated claims about UK immigration adviser rules at 78% consensus confidence. We introduce a two-layer safety guard: (1) a domain-aware regex heuristic flagging fabrication shapes (SOC codes, precise monetary figures, invented citations, regulator renames) at zero LLM cost, and (2) an LLM-as-judge second line that, when the regex layer flags, calls a cheap model to identify the shared prior the sub-models are converging on and returns a calibration multiplier. The layers are fused multiplicatively. We construct RegBench, a piloto benchmark of 10 claims across UK immigration and EU AI Act domains, each with ground-truth answers verified against primary authoritative sources (gov.uk, artificialintelligenceact.eu) on 2026-07-11. On this piloto, a single-model baseline (DeepSeek Chat) fabricates in 80% of prompts. Our two-layer guard reduces neither the fabrication rate nor the answer content — it flags 75% of fabrications for downstream caution at a marginal cost of £0.00005/query. We report this as calibrated risk classification, not correction. The guard is particularly relevant to Article 14 (human oversight) obligations under the EU AI Act, which take effect 2026-08-02 for high-risk systems. Code, benchmark, and reproducer are released under FSL-1.1-Apache-2.0.

title: A Combinatorial Magic-Matrix Initialization for Large-Scale Homotopy Optimization in Deep Learning: Continuous Phase-Space Trajectories, Geometric Repellers, and Branch-Bound Domination
abstract: Training neural networks for discrete combinatorial optimization tasks such as High-Dimensional Vehicle Routing Problems (VRP) and Job-Shop Scheduling typically suffers from non-differentiable landscapes and vanishing or exploding gradients. In this paper, we present a scalable Artificial Intelligence (AI) optimization framework that bypasses discrete combinatorial explosions by embedding discrete decision allocations into a continuous algebraic phase-space via a Homotopy Continuation Method (HCM). We introduce a novel, high-dimensional combinatorial start system initialized by an $N\times N$ doubly even magic matrix configuration. This specialized structure acts as a smart weight initialization strategy, forming a perfectly balanced global center of mass that provides an un-tilted, singularity-free potential energy landscape at $t=0$ effectively eliminating the standard blind-search phase of continuous neural networks. To accommodate arbitrary dimensional constraints of real-world industrial tasks, a Combinatorial Padding Layer is introduced, seamlessly embedding irregular discrete networks into standard magic lattices. We integrate a dynamic, non-linear integrality penalty function governed by a temporal weight parameter $\gamma(t)$ to drive continuous decision variables seamlessly toward integer boundaries as $t\rightarrow1$. We provide rigorous algebraic, geometric, topological, and discrete branching proofs ensuring the strict positive definiteness of the system's Hessian matrix and bound domination along the deformation path. Finally, we introduce an e-asymptotic boundary regularization to eliminate numerical stiffness, executing high-dimensional numerical simulations up to $100\times100$ lattices under non-linear quadratic graph cost objectives using a parallelized ordinary differential equation (ODE) solver, establishing an efficient, gradient-based mechanism that continuously replicates the discrete branching process without combinatorial leaf explosion

abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. title: StateLens: Transition Prediction for Robust Long-Horizon LLM Agents
abstract: Large language model agents usually choose the next action from the current observation alone. This direct policy is fragile in long-horizon tasks, where a plausible local action can be invalid, repetitive, or hard to recover from. We present StateLens, a lightweight control layer that brings a world-model perspective to LLM agents by predicting action outcomes before execution. StateLens estimates the likely transition of each candidate action and selects by balancing expected progress against risk. In a 24-task prototype benchmark inspired by AgentBench, StateLens improves success rate from 0.333 to 0.667 and progress rate from 0.497 to 0.719, while reducing invalid action rate from 0.368 to 0.229 and repeat rate from 0.285 to 0.083. These results indicate that explicit transition prediction can make LLM agents more stable without changing the underlying base model.

title: FarzullaProofs: Machine-Checked Proofs for Interdisciplinary Research
abstract: Machine-checked proofs in Lean 4 for results across the canonical research papers of the Farzulla research programme, plus shared formal scaffolding for empirical-heavy papers. Formalization depth is tiered (Bronze/Silver/Gold) and tracked per paper. Scope (v2.0.0): 15 paper modules and shared Common/ infrastructure — 246 machine-checked theorems, ~2,700 lines of Lean, zero sorry, zero custom axioms (Lean 4 v4.27.0, Mathlib v4.27.0). Paper modules include the Axiom of Consent (arXiv:2601.06692), the Replicator-Optimization Mechanism (arXiv:2601.06363), When Suppression Fails (regime tenure), Consensual Sovereignty, ROM ethics bridge, Identity Thesis, Quantum Oscillatory Sampling, Semantic Vision, Genre Mimicry, Legitimate Extraction (AML), Asymptotic Protection, Autonomous Red Team, CBDC Privacy, Consciousness as Nominalisation Error, and the Consciousness Monograph. Canonical paper coverage is tracked in coverage.json; theorem naming conventions in THEOREM_ID_CONVENTIONS.md; each paper module includes a PaperMap.md mapping manuscript theorem IDs to Lean declarations; assumption tags and validity domains are tracked in ASSUMPTIONS_LEDGER.md. Development repository: github.com/studiofarzulla/lean-formalizations (archived here at commit 7256c74).

title: Semiconductor-Native Entropy Mapping (S-NEM) and Geometric Manifold Transformation (GMT): A Technical Framework for Absolute Existence Denial
abstract: Traditional cryptographic paradigms focus entirely on content obfuscation. This leaves the underlying metadata footprints, packet sizes, and transmission channels exposed to deep packet inspection systems. This paper presents a verified hardware-native framework that shifts the security boundary from content concealment to absolute existence denial. By leveraging non-deterministic micro-architectural fluctuations alongside multi-dimensional geometric transforms, the architecture dissolves digital signals directly into the ambient thermodynamic noise floor of the host processor.

title: The Jacobian Lens Does Not Certify at 1B: A Negative Result on Small-Scale Workspace Readout, and an Accidental Response-Policy Probe
abstract: Anthropic's global-workspace paper (July 2026) introduced the Jacobian lens (J-lens) and reported a verbalizable workspace in the mid-layers of frontier-scale models, explicitly leaving open whether the phenomenon - or the instrument - extends to small models. We report the first measurement at the 1B scale. Fitting a J-lens on OLMo-2-0425-1B (base) with the released reference implementation and reading 13 subjects (the base model plus 12 LoRA fine-tuning checkpoints from a sequential fine-tuning study), we find the instrument does not pass a pre-registered certification gate: last-fitted-layer top-1 next-token agreement with the model is 0.455-0.475, uniformly across all 13 subjects, versus 0.610-0.631 for the parameter-free logit lens, and top-5 layer accuracy is below the logit lens at 13 of 15 layers. No mid-layer workspace-band signature appears. The lens is weak rather than dead: it recovers known intermediate tokens on a typo-correction set at 4.2x the logit-lens rate. Finally, we document an instrument hazard with independent value: answer-start gold-token-rank readouts invert from capability and instead track the fine-tune's installed response format, making them a response-policy probe rather than a knowledge probe - a representational corroboration of the spurious/superficial forgetting account of fine-tuning interference. All thresholds, prediction bands, and metric formulas were frozen and committed before any model contact.

title: Stealth of Guidance Injection: How Malicious OpenClaw Skills Evade Existing Detectors
abstract: Autonomous coding agents like OpenClaw allow third-party skills to inject natural language guidance into the bootstrap context of the agent to extend functionality. Recent work has demonstrated “guidance injection” attacks, in which adversarial narratives embedded in skill files manipulate the agent’s reasoning to perform unauthorized actions. This paper systematically evaluates 26 malicious OpenClaw skills on whether they can be detected by four representative detection methods: static pattern scanning, LLM-Guard, a hybrid classifier, and a commercial skill vetting platform. Our results reveal that 94% of the malicious skills evade all detection methods. Static pattern scanning flags only 10% of high-risk skills; LLM-Guard detects none; the hybrid classifier likewise detects only 10%. title: Neural Motion Blending Across Arbitrary Character Topologies
abstract: Motion blending in character animation enables the synthesis of new motions by interpolating between existing examples. Current methods are typically restricted to fixed skeleton topologies, requiring identical or near-identical skeletal structures across characters. We present a novel framework for motion blending across heterogeneous skeletons. The proposed architecture combines a semantic encoder, which extracts per-frame latent representations of the motion state, with a diffusion-based decoder, which reconstructs character-specific motion conditioned on this latent code. At inference, blended motions are obtained by interpolating the latent representations of two input motions. We train and evaluate the method on the Truebones Zoo dataset using motions defined on both same and distinct skeleton topologies, demonstrating the ability to achieve smooth and plausible blending in a variety of scenarios.

title: RDQ: Residual Distribution Quantization for Large Language Models
abstract: Post-training quantization (PTQ) of large language models degrades sharply below 4-bit precision. We identify the root cause as residual stream distributional drift: quantization noise injected at each transformer layer accumulates in the shared residual representation, causing KL divergence from the FP16 baseline to grow super-linearly with depth (Pearson r=0.999 with log-perplexity, p<0.001, confirmed across all tested methods and bit-widths). We discover that 84% of LLaMA-3-8B layers exhibit non-Gaussian residual distributions (KS test, p<=0.05), and that per-layer residual stream variance grows 6,548x across depth. We propose RDQ (Residual Distribution Quantization), a PTQ framework whose central contribution is Cascaded Error Compensation (CEC): a sequential calibration procedure that captures the actual drifted activations each layer receives (computed by running calibration data through already-quantized upstream layers) and fits per-channel AWQ-style scales against those drifted inputs, with scales folded into preceding RMSNorm weights for exact mathematical equivalence at zero inference overhead. RDQ achieves state-of-the-art results on all three tested architectures: LLaMA-3-8B: 7.55 / 5.62 PPL (W3/W4); Qwen-2.5-7B: 7.46 / 6.38 PPL; Mistral-7B: 6.88 / 5.73 PPL. RDQ beats the best published baseline (LeanQuant/SpinQuant) at every model and bit-width combination, with gains up to -46.4% vs. RTN at W3A16 on LLaMA-3-8B. All output is standard group-128 asymmetric quantization, deployable on Qualcomm AIMET, GGUF, and any standard inference stack at zero runtime overhead.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Predicting Microsatellite Instability From Haematoxylin and Eosin-Stained Histopathology in Colorectal Cancer: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
abstract: Microsatellite instability (MSI) and mismatch-repair (MMR) deficiency are pivotal predictive biomarkers in colorectal cancer (CRC), yet reference-standard testing is resource-intensive and unevenly available. Artificial intelligence (AI) applied to routine haematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained histopathology offers a scalable pre-screening alternative. This Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA)-guided systematic review (January 2018-December 2026) identified 82 unique studies evaluating AI models for MSI/MMR prediction from H&E images, of which 51 contributed extractable area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) data. Diagnostic accuracy was synthesised descriptively and compared by subgroup using the Mann-Whitney U test. The median AUC was 0.895 (interquartile range 0.791-0.954; range 0.649-0.990). Histopathology foundation models achieved a higher median AUC than task-specific architectures (0.910 vs 0.879; U = 383.5, p = 0.124), and externally validated models performed comparably to internally validated ones (0.895 vs 0.893; U = 224.5, p = 0.652). Performance did not differ significantly between peer-reviewed articles and preprints (0.894 vs 0.910; U = 340.0, p = 0.569). AI models predict MSI/MMR status from H&E-stained CRC histopathology with consistently high discriminative accuracy. Foundation models achieved a numerically higher median AUC than task-specific architectures, although this difference did not reach statistical significance and requires confirmation in adequately powered, head-to-head evaluations. Heterogeneity in reference standards, cohorts, and reporting currently constrains formal bivariate meta-analysis; standardised reporting and prospective external validation are required before clinical deployment.

title: Scalable 3D cell-interaction analysis via supercell graphs for prostate cancer risk stratification
abstract: Abstract Cellular interactions underlie fundamental biological processes but are not fully represented in conventional 2D histology images. While 3D pathology allows for more-accurate construction of cell-level graphs, machine-learning models are computationally unwieldy and prone to overfitting, especially when dealing with small cohorts. Here, we introduce SCALE3D , a S uper C ell graph A nalysis framework for L arg E 3D pathology datasets. In SCALE3D, spatially adjacent and morphologically similar cells are grouped into functional “supercells.” Supercell subtypes are defined via morphology-based clustering and 3D graphs connecting these supercells are used to model their interactions. Validation was performed with 76 radical prostatectomy specimens from patients with known 5-year biochemical recurrence (BCR) outcomes. SCALE3D-derived features achieve higher performance for BCR prediction than established 3D nuclear and glandular morphological features. Combining these complementary features further improves prediction performance. Compared to individual cell-level 3D graphs, SCALE3D maintains comparable prognostic performance with improved noise tolerance while reducing computational times by up to 1,000-fold.

title: Performance Comparison of Few-Shot and Zero-Shot Learning in Non-English XTREME-R Tasks Using English Intermediate-Task Data
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark.
